A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StaR research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of baseline and StaR-trained agents on the state control benchmark, three general agentic benchmarks, and 20 dynamic mobile tasks.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds GUI-Owl evaluations, prompting comparisons, annotation-quality audits, component ablations, and error analysis.

M1.justification: StaR retains the same trained perceiving, analyzing, and deciding chain, combined with refined toggle episodes and ordinary agentic training data. Appendix A.5 elaborates implementation, including handling non-toggling steps already illustrated in v1. The annotation-equation discrepancy noted under T1 does not establish an actual procedure change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six source datasets, binary toggle task, AndroidControl-H/L, AITZ, GUI-Odyssey, and 20 dynamic mobile tasks. GUIAct-Mobile specifies the earlier GUIAct source. Additional agents, prompting controls, and audits use retained task and data coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds GUI-Owl-7B and four evaluated comparison approaches: state-focused prompting, StaR-style prompting, ground-truth state prompting, and ground-truth state combined with StaR-style prompting (Tables 1 and 9). Original comparators remain; proprietary-agent results move from v1 Table 1 to v2 Table 9.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with privileged ground-truth state inputs, explicit prompting controls, component-removal training experiments, and manual assessments of 100 annotation instances and 200 disjoint benchmark instances. Existing benchmark sizes, metrics, click-distance thresholds, learning rate, and epoch count remain unchanged; newly disclosed settings do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds annotation-quality validation, OS-Atlas ablations removing perceiving or analyzing (Table 10), and analysis of 463 degradation and 287 improvement cases for AgentCPM (Appendix B.2). These address label reliability, component contributions, and failure causes absent from v1. The Wi-Fi case studies are retained and moved to Appendix B.4.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 introduces sample-based estimates of individual annotator correctness and an independence-based estimate of retained-label accuracy (Table 4), absent from v1. This adds a limited statistical estimation procedure. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for agent performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive prompting, GUI-Owl, ablation, audit, and error-analysis results. UI-TARS state-control O-AMR entries change from 45.53% to 47.45% zero-shot and from 74.52% to 77.86% with training; the PDFs do not explain these revisions. Dynamic results remain unchanged. For GUI-Owl, Table 1 implies a 24.03-point gain, conflicting with the 21.64% stated in Section 5.2.

T1.justification: v2 adds a localized annotation-reliability derivation under independent annotator correctness assumptions (Appendix A.1, Equations 5-6). Equation 1 also changes from conjunction to equality of the binary toggle indicators, admitting joint negative classifications and contradicting the retained prose. The added metric formulas otherwise restate existing definitions.

C1.justification: The principal benchmark, StaR effectiveness, generalization, and dynamic-applicability claims remain. The introduction newly claims that prompting cannot fundamentally improve toggle reasoning, strengthening the motivation for learned intrinsic reasoning. Describing StaR as a multimodal reasoning method and extending evidence to four agents do not themselves redefine its contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of why prompting fails, characterizes oracle-state baselines as upper bounds on training-free collaboration, and argues for integrating all reasoning components. Appendix B.2 newly attributes AgentCPM regressions to coordinate drift and fixed visual tokens, whereas v1 merely acknowledged lower performance. These broaden the mechanism and failure explanations substantially.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 and Table 8 substantially expand reproducibility information: full fine-tuning, unfrozen vision components, sequence length, batch size, accumulation, scheduler, warmup, precision, action-format conversion, and four-step UI-TARS history. v2 also documents source proportions, paired split membership, and additional agent and baseline prompts. These are largely new disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds related works including Insight-V, Argus, CogAgent, ShowUI, Magma, and multimodal chain-of-thought research, and foregrounds multimodal reasoning. The central positioning around improving intrinsic toggle reasoning instead of relying on external annotation remains, making this a limited expansion of research positioning.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten and condensed. Reasoning-related work moves ahead of the other related-work subsections, terminology changes from toggle feature to functionality, case studies move into the appendix, and the experimental appendices receive substantial restructuring and expanded explanations.

P2.justification: v2 changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, redesigns Figure 1, expands Figure 3 with a prompting panel and consistently oriented axes, and reorganizes general-agent plots. It expands comparison tables and adds data-source, audit, action-space, hyperparameter, and ablation tables. Existing case-study figures and prompt displays are relocated or resized.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence and reproducibility where v1 lacked prompting controls, component tests, and empirical label validation. Tables 9-10 directly examine alternatives and reasoning components, while Appendix A adds annotation audits and detailed training settings. These gains outweigh the new annotation-equation inconsistency, numerical reporting errors, and overly broad oracle upper-bound claims, which still limit confidence in some interpretations.
